context: In the proofs of both Theorem 2 and Theorem 3, the “if” direction requires to provide update formulas for all regular languages whose (ordered) syntactic monoids satisfy some property and is standard. The “only-if” direction requires to prove lower bounds against DynProp (resp. UDynΣ+ 1 ) for all non-group languages (resp. all languages whose ordered syntactic monoid is not in J+ ∗ G). To this end we prove a lower bound for a single language using variants of the Substructure lemma [4] (see also [20]) and lift this lower bounds to all languages without the property using algebraic insights. We leave open the question to find a precise algebraic characterization of languages in UDynΣ1 , i.e., languages maintainable by (not necessarily positive) ∃∗ -formulas and unary auxiliary relations. We discuss challenges towards answering this question in Section 6. 2 Preliminaries In this section, also to fix notation, we recall basics of dynamic descriptive complexity and algebraic formal language theory. 2.1 Dynamic descriptive complexity In this paper, we are interested in the dynamic membership problem for fixed regular languages. Let L ⊆ Σ∗ be a language over some alphabet Σ. The input structure for the dynamic membership problem Member(L) of L is an encoding of a word w = w1 · · · wn as a relational structure over the domain {1, . . . , n} of the positions of the word. This structure has (1) for every σ ∈ Σ a unary relation Wσ for storing the positions of w that contain σ and (2) a binary relation ≤ representing the linear order of the positions of w. Following Patnaik and Immerman as well as Gelade et al. [10, 4], each wi is either in Σ or ϵ, i.e., each position i ∈ [n] can occur in at most one relation Wσ . For the sake of simplicity, we denote both input words and their encoding by the same symbol w.

statement: We characterized the regular languages of UDynΣ+1 and UDynProp by properties of their (ordered) syntactic monoids. The most important fragment of DynFO for which a characterization remains open is UDynΣ1 (see also the discussion in the full version of this paper).
context: 6 Conclusion We characterized the regular languages of UDynΣ+1 and UDynProp by properties of their (ordered) syntactic monoids. The most important fragment of DynFO for which a characterization remains open is UDynΣ1 (see also the discussion in the full version of this paper). ▶ Open question. Which regular languages are in UDynΣ1 , i.e. can be maintained by ∃∗ update formulas and unary auxiliary relations? Two obstacles to an algebraic characterization of UDynΣ1 are (1) that Σ1 is not closed under composition and thus UDynΣ1 is a priori not a (positive) variety; and (2) an absence of lower bounds techniques against UDynΣ1 . One path towards resolving (1) is via considering positive lp-varieties, which only require closure under positive Boolean operations and under quotients of inverses of length-preserving morphisms [14]. For (2), new lower bound techniques beyond the substructure lemma (and its variant used for UDynΣ+ 1 ) seem to be necessary.

The most important fragment of DynFO for which a characterization remains open is UDynΣ1 (see also the discussion in the full version of this paper). ▶ Open question. Two obstacles to an algebraic characterization of UDynΣ1 are (1) that Σ1 is not closed under composition and thus UDynΣ1 is a priori not a (positive) variety; and (2) an absence of lower bounds techniques against UDynΣ1 . Consider the class J of languages that can be described by a Boolean combination of Σ1 -formulas. This class is equal to the class of piecewise-testable languages [18]. We can show that UDynΣ1 is strictly more powerful than UDynΣ+ + 1 , by looking at the unordered counterpart of J ∗ G.

context: Unfortunately, J ∗ G does not provide an exact characterization, because the language Σ∗ aaΣ∗ is in UDynΣ1 , but its ordered syntactic monoid is not in J ∗ G. ▶ Conjecture 37. Let V be the positive lp-variety of regular languages L such that Member(L) is in UDynΣ1 . Then J ∗ G ⊊ V ⊆ Σ2 ∗ G. In particular, (Σ∗ aaΣ∗ )c is not5 in V. Another direction is to explore (fragments of) the class of context-free languages. It is known that every context-free language can be maintained in DynFO [4], yet the known dynamic program requires Σ1 -update formulas and 4-ary auxiliary relations. ▶ Open question. Which dynamic resources (quantifier-alterations, arity of auxiliary relations,. . . ) are required for maintaining context-free languages?
